https://techxplore.com/news/2018-07-dubai-vertical-farming-quench-thirst.html

Crop One and Emirates Flight Catering (EKFC) have launched a $40 million joint venture to build the world's largest vertical farming facility in Dubai, United Arab Emirates.

Growing food inside, not outdoors, means no pesticides or herbicides or fungicides because every aspect of the growing environment is controlled. Crop One's CEO claims to have reduced per unit cost greatly compared to competitors and they make a profit. They use 18,000 gallons of water a year in one of these units while one would need 46 million gallons of water in the field to grow the same amount of food in that same year.

The vertical farm facility will cover 130,000 square feet—with a production output equivalent to 900 acres of farmland.

The facility will go under construction near the Al Maktoum International Airport.

Locating it near the airport is an example of one of the advantages of vertical farms, in that they can be built anywhere in any climate, and here the proximity of the farm to point of consumption means less carbon emissions from transportation. Emirates Flight Catering's customers include 105 airlines and 25 airport lounges.

The construction gets under way in November, and the facility will take about a year to complete.

The vertical farm in New Jersey, USA is currently the largest in the world. Competition will help the vertical farming industry to reduce costs further and spur innovation. I'm all for that.
